scale: venue proof (24 jobs, Mistral, batch tier — fourth venue to capture)
notes: The fourth venue to capture. 24/24 ok, zero sync fallbacks, 50.0% captured, 33 seconds end to end on mistral-small-latest — the same twenty-four-line book that 2026-08-26-mistral-2 reached and threw away ninety minutes earlier.

Nothing about the venue changed between the two rows. The batch in mistral-2 also succeeded, 24/24, in 6m16s; what changed is that offpeak can now read the output file it was already being handed. MistralBatch._download reached for a streaming response's .text before reading it, which raises httpx.ResponseNotRead — a RuntimeError, so the getattr(..., None) guard around it never applied. collect() raised, run() booked the finished batch as a polling failure, and every job took the sync fallback at list.

So the pair is the evidence, not this row alone. mistral-1 (402) was a venue refusing the tier. mistral-2 was the tier reached, billed and discarded by a client bug. mistral-3 is the tier reached and kept. All three stay on the ledger: the two that captured nothing are why the one that captured is worth believing.

Cheapest row on the board tonight by a wide margin — $0.0000999 paid across 24 jobs — because mistral-small answers a one-word question in four tokens and is priced at $0.15/$0.60 per million. Sub-cent is the point; production volume is a different claim and is not made here.
